prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production 2D animation sprite sheet for the reference character only. Inés, auburn braided hair, orange construction jacket, purple scarf, gray trousers and work boots. Holds rectangular blue-and-white scrap road-sign shield in left hand and red rusted crowbar in right hand. Reference sheet shows the exact identity, outfit, face, proportions and comic rendering to retain. NEW sheet: exactly TWENTY FOUR full-body sequential drawings in a perfectly regular SIX columns by FOUR rows grid, landscape 3:2 canvas 1536x1024. Read left-to-right then next row. Each of the 24 cells is equal sized, no borders, no captions, no numbers, no shadows, genuinely transparent background. Character faces RIGHT in three-quarter side view, stays fully inside EACH cell, same camera, same size and two boots planted on the EXACT SAME baseline in ALL cells. American action comic, crisp black inks, vivid flat workwear colors and hard cel-shading, NOT pixel art or painterly blur. Animate a very subtle natural ready-to-fight guard: slow breathing in chest, slight elbow bends lift hands and weapon a little then return, mild knee flex WITHOUT moving boots, hair tips and loose cloth hems wave gently backwards in wind. Frame 1 neutral, frame 12 maximum inhale/guard raise, frame 24 smoothly returns almost to frame 1. Small incremental changes between neighbors, no attack, no weapon swapping, no rotation, no walking, no floating, no perspective shifts, no duplicate extra limbs, no growth/shrinking. Every cell a distinct coherent in-between. Weapon and hands move together. Prioritize animation continuity over pose variety. No background or solid cell rectangles, true alpha surrounding each drawing.
NEW FINAL ART DIRECTION: original printed American action COMIC BOOK, this is a full REDRAW of the illustration. Strong expressive black ink outlines, angular purposeful shapes, two-tone cel shadows, vivid controlled hero accents on a dark violet/steel/petrol palette, visible Ben-Day halftone clusters and occasional dry ink. A clear THIN WHITE PAPER CUTOUT border around every person, machine, standalone object and icon silhouette. Comics cut-paper aesthetic, NOT 3D, NOT realistic painting, NOT pixel art, NOT generic airbrushed fantasy. Civilian survivors versus autonomous killing machines; retain their identities, jobs, workwear and improvised tools. No superhero costumes. The illustration must visibly feel like hand-inked printed comic art.
